Fig. \ref{f.sim.4} compares the EE performance under different MM-RIS configurations, including cases with 
(1) fully optimized MM-RIS; 
(2) half EH capability, i.e., half elements are with $\alpha_{q,m}=0.5$; 
(3) without signal amplification $\beta_{q,m}^{k}=1$;
(4) without EH functionality of $\alpha_{q,m}=1$; 
(5) half EH and without amplification $\beta_{q,m}^{k}=1$; 
(6) without both EH and amplification; 
(7) reflection-only operation. 
The results indicate that when EH is disabled, the EE initially exhibits a slight improvement with an increasing number of elements, but subsequently declines significantly. This trend implies that additional MM-RIS elements initially provide enhanced array and beamforming gains, whereas excessive elements introduce substantially higher operational power consumption associated with movement, control, and signal amplification, which eventually dominates the achievable rate gain and degrades EE. In contrast, enabling EH provides significantly higher EE than the corresponding non-EH configurations because the harvested energy can partially compensate for the additional element-dependent power consumption and support active signal amplification. However, as the number of MM-RIS elements continues to increase, the incremental harvested energy may become insufficient to compensate for the increasing operational expenditure, resulting in a decline in EE. The crossover points among different MM-RIS configurations further reveal this competing relationship. For a relatively small number of elements, configurations with signal amplification can achieve higher EE because the amplification gain effectively compensates for severe channel attenuation and provides a substantial rate improvement relative to its additional power consumption. However, as the number of elements increases, the accumulated amplification and movement power grows, whilst the marginal communication gain gradually diminishes. As a result, configurations with partial or disabled amplification may become comparably more energy-efficient, leading to intersections among the corresponding EE curves. Similarly, EH shifts these crossover points by offsetting part of the increased operational power, allowing EH-enabled configurations to maintain their EE advantage over a wider range of element numbers. These crossings indicate that no single MM-RIS operating mode is uniformly optimal for all cases of $M$. Alternatively, the preferred configuration depends on the compelling balance among array gains, amplification gains, harvested energy, and element power consumption. For the half-EH case, the system achieves improved EE by leveraging partially harvested energy to support signal amplification with $\beta_{q,m}^k>1$, thereby outperforming its counterpart without amplification over most of the considered operating range. Without amplification, the MM-RIS behaves similarly to a passive metasurface and cannot effectively compensate for severe channel fading, resulting in reduced EE performance. Furthermore, the "No EH and No Amp." baseline generally exhibits the lowest EE among the STAR-capable MM-RIS configurations because both energy harvesting and active signal enhancement are disabled, effectively degenerating into a conventional passive STAR structure. Additionally, in the reflection-only RIS case, the transmitted signals cannot effectively serve users located on the opposite side of the surface, resulting in substantial EE degradation due to its limited half-space coverage. In contrast, the proposed MM-RIS simultaneously supports signal reflection and transmission, amplification, and EH, thereby providing full-space coverage while adaptively balancing communication enhancement and energy expenditure.

Fig. \ref{f.sim.7} depicts the EE performance under different numbers of users. We compare the proposed hybrid RSMA-NOMA transmissions to the existing multiple access mechanisms, including RSMA \cite{2}, NOMA \cite{44}, spatial division multiple access (SDMA), and OMA. For conventional RSMA, the private streams are decoded without SIC, whereas the common stream is decoded first and removed before decoding the intended private stream. For the NOMA benchmark, the common streams of RSMA are disabled, and only the private streams are transmitted using power-domain multiplexing with SIC. For SDMA, the SIC operation is disabled, and the users are simultaneously served through spatial transmission. Accordingly, when decoding the signal intended for $U_{kj}$, the signals intended for all other users $i\in\mathcal{J}_k$, $i\neq j$, within the same group are treated as interference without cancellation. For OMA, time-division mechanism is adopted, i.e., the available transmission time is orthogonally divided among all users, such that only one user is served within each
allocated time fraction. Note that all methods are optimized based solely on CRAFTS, differing only in their multiple access mechanisms. As the number of users increases, the EE of all mechanisms gradually decreases due to intensified inter-user interference and limited power resources in denser environments. The proposed hybrid RSMA-NOMA scheme achieves the highest EE across all benchmarks, benefiting from the synergistic integration of RSMA and NOMA. This is because RSMA effectively mitigates inter-user interference through message splitting and common-stream decoding, whereas NOMA further improves spectral efficiency via power-domain multiplexing and SIC. Comparably, pure RSMA achieves moderate EE owing to its robust interference management capability, whereas NOMA outperforms SDMA and OMA due to its higher spectral utilization. However, the performance of NOMA degrades as the SIC process becomes increasingly sensitive to interference accumulation in denser user scenarios. Meanwhile, SDMA suffers from limited spatial DoFs, whereas OMA exhibits the lowest EE due to inefficient orthogonal resource allocation. To elaborate a little further, the residual interference may take place owing to the imperfect SIC process, i.e., the term of $\iota \cdot \| \mathbf{g}_{kj} \mathbf{f}_k^p \|^2 \sum\limits_{i\in\mathcal{J}_k, i<j} p_{ki}$ exists owing to imperfect SIC, expressed in the denominator of private SINR in \eqref{SIC_decode}. Note that the residual interference coefficient is set to $\iota=0.3$. Although EE values of both hybrid RSMA-NOMA and pure NOMA transmissions decrease under imperfect SIC, the proposed hybrid multiple access still maintains substantial EE advantages and even outperforms the perfect SIC versions of standalone RSMA and NOMA. This result indicates that the message-splitting structure of RSMA effectively alleviates residual interference and suppresses SIC error propagation.

EE initially improves with increasing velocity owing to enhanced rate, but gradually saturates or decreases at high velocities when the movement power dominates the rate gain. Such a phenomenon is particularly noticeable for the cases with longer communication durations, i.e., $T=4$. Furthermore, larger transmission durations achieve substantially higher EE and sum-rate as movement overhead can be alleviated over a longer communication interval to fully exploit the channel enhancement. In contrast, when $T \in \{1,2\}$, EE and sum-rate degrade significantly as the repositioning may occupy a considerable portion of the transmission block. In addition, EE and sum-rate of $D=\lambda$  become lower compared to $D=\lambda/2$ as large spacing limits MEs from approaching favorable channels. Meanwhile, when $D=\lambda/4$, the system also experiences performance degradation despite the increased movement flexibility. This result is potentially caused by the spatial correlation among closely spaced elements, which reduces channel diversity gains. 
\subsection{Effect of MM-RIS Deployment Strategy}

\caption{EE performance with various deployment ranges and strategies.} \label{f.sim.13}

Fig. \ref{f.sim.13} illustrates EE with different numbers of MM-RISs under various deployment policies. As observed, all schemes exhibit a concave trend, where EE initially increases with more MM-RISs and reaches its peak around four surfaces, followed by a gradual decline. This result indicates that deploying additional MM-RISs can effectively improve spatial diversity and communication coverage during the initial deployment. However, excessive MM-RIS deployments introduce substantial operational overhead for both the surfaces and MEs in terms of time and power consumption, which dominates the achievable rate gains and reduces the overall EE performance. Moreover, large deployment range of $35$ m provides higher spatial deployment flexibility compared to the other cases, allowing MM-RISs to dynamically locate more appropriate positions for improving channel conditions. Note that the fixed deployment uniformly distributes the MM-RISs within a deployment region of $35$ m, whereas the random case randomly places the MM-RISs within a coverage radius of $35$ m. It can be inferred that both policies achieve lower EE compared to the optimized deployment strategies due to the absence of adaptive deployment optimization. Nevertheless, both random and fixed deployments outperform the optimized deployment with a range of $15$ m. This is because a wider deployment region, even without explicit optimization, can still provide a higher probability of locating MM-RISs near favorable communication regions and better channel conditions.
\subsection{Impact of User Grouping Mechanisms}
\begin{figure}[!t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\figsize in]{fig/Figure_17.eps}
\caption{Comparison of different user grouping mechanisms.} \label{f.sim.17}
\end{figure}
Fig. \ref{f.sim.17} investigates the impact of the number of user groups $K$, also referred to as $K$ directions, on the system EE under different grouping strategies. As $K$ increases
from $2$ to $4$, the EE of all schemes improves. This is because partitioning the users into more groups reduces the number of users multiplexed within each group, which is capable of alleviating intra-group interference. However, further increasing $K$ degrades the EE. With an excessive number of groups, more group-specific transmissions compete for the available communication resources and the resulting inter-group interference becomes more pronounced. Therefore, an intermediate number of groups provides a favorable balance between intra-group multiplexing and inter-group interference, with $K=4$ achieving the highest EE performance. Moreover, the channel-aware grouping scheme outperforms the distance-based and random grouping schemes for all considered values of $K$. This improvement is owing to the grouping users with highly correlated effective channel directions, which facilitates efficient beamforming, whereas the subsequent channel-gain-based user ordering supports effective NOMA SIC. In contrast, distance-based grouping only exploits geographical proximity and therefore does not necessarily capture the effective channel information. Random grouping does not exploit either channel or spatial information, leading to the lowest EE performance.
\subsection{Benchmark Comparison}
\begin{figure}[!t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\figsize in]{fig/Figure_9.eps}
\caption{Ablation studies of EE under different parameter configurations.} \label{f.sim.12}

We conduct ablation studies of the proposed fully optimized scheme by CRAFTS in terms of EE performance across different baseline methods in Fig. \ref{f.sim.12}. Note that "w/o" indicates that the parameters are not optimized and randomly allocated. It reveals that the EE performance firstly escalates with an increasing number of antennas owing to the enhanced beamforming capability, followed by a peak at $N=6$. Then, EE declines as the total power consumption dominates the beamforming gains. To elaborate a little further, increasing $N$ enlarges the available beamforming DoFs and can potentially improve the achievable rate. However, the additional antennas at the BS also introduce antenna-dependent power consumption. Hence, assigning zero transmit power to an additional antenna does not completely eliminate its associated power consumption. As $N$ increases, the marginal beamforming and achievable rate gains become insufficient to compensate for the additional power consumption, resulting in the observed EE degradation beyond $N=6$. It is evident that the full optimization yields the highest EE, while omitting the optimization of specific parameters leads to noticeable EE degradation. Crucially, the configuration without optimizing BS beamforming results in the lowest EE performance of around $0.4$ bits/J as the active beamforming at BS is the fundamental prerequisite for establishing the primary link. Moreover, the random EH scheme also exhibits substantial EE degradation owing to inefficient energy allocation and insufficient harvested energy to support active component operations. Particularly, the random surface deployment has much lower EE than the case of the ME position adjustment, emphasizing the compelling importance of large-scale fading over small-scale fading. Meanwhile, the case without phase-shift optimization has lower EE than the random amplification benchmark, further confirming the importance of MM-RIS-based beam alignment.

Fig. \ref{f.sim.15} evaluates the EE performance of the proposed CRAFTS framework against several benchmarks under different numbers of antennas at BS, including HDRL-BiPS \cite{31}, HDRL \cite{han}, conventional beamforming methods of zero-forcing \cite{zf} and minimum mean square error (MMSE) \cite{mmse}, heuristic optimization using genetic algorithm \cite{ga}, and random configurations. Among all schemes, the proposed CRAFTS framework achieves the highest EE performance across all antenna numbers. This superiority stems from the synergistic integration of hybrid DRL, FL, transformer, and adaptive Lagrangian optimization. Comparably, the HDRL-BiPS scheme achieves the second-best EE due to the incorporation of the proposed bi-directional parameterized sharing mechanism, enabling information exchange between continuous and discrete action branches. However, without FL and transformer enhancement, its capability to handle highly-coupled variables remains limited. Meanwhile, the conventional HDRL scheme further suffers from reduced coordination capability and weaker feature extraction, leading to much lower EE than HDRL-BiPS. Furthermore, conventional beamforming methods exhibit substantially lower EE than DRL-based schemes since they only optimize BS beamforming without jointly coordinating MM-RIS components. Interestingly, the heuristic method achieves relatively poor EE despite its iterative optimization capability. This is because heuristic search often suffers from high computational complexity and limited adaptability in dynamic environments, making them more susceptible to converging toward local optimal solutions. Finally, the random scheme achieves the lowest EE performance and serves as the performance lower bound.

\section{Conclusions} \label{sec_con}
	We have proposed an MM-RIS-assisted hybrid RSMA-NOMA architecture by deploying ME-enhanced MF-RISs to enable EE-oriented joint communication and spatial optimization under stringent QoS, power budget, and self-sustainability constraints. To solve the high-dimensional mixed discrete-continuous and non-convex problem, we have proposed a CRAFTS framework incorporating a transformer-based feature extraction architecture and a hybrid DRL structure combining MAPPO and MADQN. The FL and bi-directional parametrized sharing mechanisms are designed to enhance learning stability and improve multi-agent coordination under highly coupled optimization variables. Furthermore, an adaptive primal-dual Lagrangian-based scheme is conceived to dynamically regulate constraint violations and ensure reliable constraint satisfaction. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed CRAFTS framework substantially outperforms both existing centralized and decentralized DRL benchmarks, conventional precoding methods, as well as heuristic optimization approaches. The results also reveal an important trade-off between communication enhancement and the operational overhead of ME-based systems, where excessive amplification, movement flexibility, or surface deployment may eventually increase power consumption and reduce EE performance. Moreover, the proposed MM-RIS-assisted hybrid RSMA-NOMA achieves superior EE across several system configurations, including imperfect SIC conditions, fixed-EH configurations, conventional RIS architectures, and baselines without amplification, EH, or ME optimization. To elaborate further, the proposed CRAFTS framework substantially outperforms both existing centralized and decentralized DRL benchmarks, conventional precoding methods as well as heuristic optimization approaches in the open literature.
From a practical implementation perspective, CRAFTS does not require retraining for every instantaneous channel realization. The policy can be trained offline over diverse channel and user realizations and then employed for low-latency online inference. Nevertheless, its generalization performance may degrade under substantial distribution shifts in user locations or propagation environments that are not sufficiently represented during training, in which case policy fine-tuning or retraining may be required. Furthermore, a multi-timescale implementation is more suitable for rapidly varying channels, where beamforming, power allocation, and electronic MM-RIS configurations are adapted on a relatively fast timescale, while MM-RIS deployment and ME repositioning are updated on a slower timescale according to user mobility and large-scale channel variations. Developing transfer, meta-learning, and continual learning mechanisms for rapid adaptation to previously unseen environments constitutes an important direction for future work. Furthermore, incorporating heterogeneous movement velocities, energy consumption, and reconfiguration delays of panel-level deployment and element-level repositioning into a multi timescale optimization framework constitutes an important direction for future studies.

paper.title: Conformal Risk Control for Multiuser Beamforming
paper.abstract: We consider multiuser downlink beamforming with prescribed signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) requirements under imperfect channel state information and a tight transmit power budget. Robust worst-case designs often require tractable channel-error models and may not yield feasible beamformers that meet the power budget. To alleviate these issues, we propose conformal risk control for beamforming (CRCBeam), which combines the classical fixed-point minimum-power beamforming with conformal risk control to calibrate an SINR margin from calibration sample pairs of estimated and true channels. Under exchangeability, CRCBeam provides finite-sample control over served-outage risk, which is the probability of transmitting when at least one user fails to meet its SINR target. CRCBeam requires no parametric channel-error model and transmits only when the power budget is met. Numerical experiments using a pilot contamination channel error model corroborate that CRCBeam achieves the served-outage risk while meeting the power budget. In contrast, worst-case robust baselines, Gaussian-ball and conformal-ball beamforming, either do not meet the target risk or exceed the power budget.

paper.title: ARISE: Adaptive Agentic Reasoning with Image-grounded Self-Evaluation for Interpretable IBD Assessment
paper.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) requires frequent imaging-based assessment, yet interpretation of modalities such as wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) and intestinal ultrasound remains heavily dependent on specialist expertise. Vision-Language Models (VLMs) demonstrate significant potential in multimodal medical image analysis, but their clinical adoption is hindered by their insufficient domain-specific reasoning, susceptibility to hallucination, scarcity of high quality training data in fine-grained diagnostics and limited interpretability. We introduce ARISE (Adaptive Agentic Reasoning with Image-grounded Self-Evaluation), an autonomous planning framework that models few-shot medical image understanding as a sequential agentic workflow. ARISE structures agent execution into a transparent 5-stage workflow: hypothesis generation, image-grounded evidence summarization, evidence-conditioned refinement, symbolic verification, and final diagnosis. We apply ARISE to IBD assessment across two independent patient cohorts: wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) images for Crohn's disease and B-mode ultrasound data for ulcerative colitis. ARISE consistently improves diagnostic performance over baseline VLMs while exposing where reasoning succeeds or fails, providing a more interpretable basis for clinical decision support and realistic deployment.

paper.title: EchoDino: A pediatric foundation model for transferable echocardiographic analysis across the lifespan
paper.abstract: Echocardiography is the most widely used cardiac imaging modality, yet interpretation demands integrating visual evidence across global anatomy, localized structures and dynamic cardiac motion. Machine-learning models have automated individual tasks, but they are typically built for a single purpose and depend on expensively labeled datasets - a barrier particularly acute in pediatric care, where data are scarce and anatomy changes with age. Here we present EchoDino, a self-supervised foundation model for echocardiography, created by adapting the DINOv3 framework to 3.7 million frames from 1.7 million unlabeled pediatric echocardiography videos. With its encoder frozen, EchoDino produces representations that capture global context, local anatomy, and dense spatial detail. We introduce Motion-biased Entropy Maximization Sampling (MEMS) to select the most informative frames for video-level analysis. Across nine pediatric and adult datasets, EchoDino outperformed strong baseline models, raising view-classification accuracy from 0.609 to 0.889 and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for structural-heart-disease detection from 0.811 to 0.872, while also cutting age-estimation error from 3.857 to 1.389 years, achieving the best segmentation accuracy and lowering ejection-fraction errors. By generalizing from label-free pediatric data to adult echocardiography, EchoDino offers a versatile foundation for cardiac image analysis across the lifespan.

paper.title: Robust Design of Sensing-Assisted Secure Transmission for RIS-Aided ISAC System under Eavesdropper 3D Positioning Uncertainty
paper.abstract: Localization errors in estimating the position of a potential eavesdropper (Eve) pose a critical challenge to secure transmission in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. To address this issue, this paper proposes a sensing-assisted robust secure transmission framework that exploits ISAC sensing to characterize the positioning uncertainty induced by these errors. The RIS is partitioned into a reflection region and a sensing reception region, supporting sensing and communication through spatial separation. By jointly exploiting observations collected at the base station (BS) and the RIS sensing reception region, maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) is employed to estimate the arrival angles, from which Eve's three-dimensional (3D) position is obtained through cross localization. The resulting localization Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) is then used to construct an ellipsoidal uncertainty region around the estimated position. A two-stage optimization strategy is developed. In Stage I, the sensing beamformer and RIS reflection coefficients are jointly optimized to improve localization accuracy. In Stage II, the resulting positioning uncertainty is incorporated into a robust secure transmission design, where the communication beamformer and RIS reflection coefficients are jointly optimized to maximize the worst-case secrecy rate. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms benchmark schemes without RIS assistance and with random RIS configurations in terms of secrecy performance. The proposed framework effectively mitigates secrecy performance degradation caused by localization errors in Eve's position.

paper.title: Decouple, Purify and Unite: Semantic-Structural Prototype Learning for Federated Medical Segmentation
paper.abstract: Federated learning enables medical institutions to train a global model without sharing data, yet feature heterogeneity from diverse scanners or protocols remains challenging. Existing representation-based methods face two limitations: 1) Incomplete Contextual Representation Learning: single-layer or coupled representations overlook multi-level structural cues and entangle regional semantics with boundary details. 2) Layerwise Style and Aggregation Biases: domain-specific style discrepancies across intermediate layers degrade prototypes, while aggregation that overlooks client distribution shifts can further amplify bias. We propose FedBCS+, federated decoupled contextual alignment with style-purified aggregation. We employ Frequency-domain Style Recalibration (FSR) in prototype construction to decouple content-style representations and extract style-purified prototypes. Built upon these purified features, Decoupled Contextual Prototype Alignment (DCPA) explicitly decouples multi-level features into semantic and structural prototypes and aligns regional semantics and fine-grained anatomical structures separately. Style-purified Semantic Prototype Aggregation (S2PA) measures each client's purified prototype divergence from the global consensus and adaptively reweights aggregation toward under-represented clients to reduce consensus bias. On five heterogeneous medical segmentation benchmarks spanning histopathology, MRI, ultrasound, and colonoscopy, FedBCS+ achieves the highest mean Dice among the compared methods. A convergence analysis further characterizes how aggregation and alignment affect the optimization bound.

paper.title: UAV Rotatable Antenna under Rotation Delay
paper.abstract: Rotatable antennas (RAs) can improve wireless link performance by adjusting their boresight directions. However, existing RA studies generally assume instantaneous antenna reconfiguration, whereas mechanical rotation incurs non-negligible delay in practical deployment. To address this issue, we develop a rotation-delay-aware communication model for finite communication slots, where mechanical rotation directly reduces the time available for data transmission. This model reveals a fundamental tradeoff between the communication gain achieved through RA reorientation and the associated transmission-time loss. Accordingly, we formulate a rotation-delay-aware joint design of RA orientations and transmit beamforming to maximize the minimum effective transmission rate. For the single-user system, under a sufficient condition for strict concavity, the global optimum falls into one of three regimes: no rotation, partial rotation, and full rotation. A closed-form approximation is derived using a second-order expansion. For the multi-user system, we separate rotation-budget selection from fixed-budget max-min signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) optimization. An analytic-gradient zero-forcing (AG-ZF) algorithm is then developed for low-complexity joint RA orientation and rotation-budget optimization. The results show that explicitly accounting for mechanical rotation delay is essential for finite-slot RA-enabled UAV communications, and that the proposed designs effectively balance reconfiguration gain and transmission-time loss while achieving favorable effective-rate performance with low computational complexity.

paper.title: Beyond Explanation: Debugging Medical Imaging Models via Concept Intervention
paper.abstract: Medical imaging models often operate as black boxes, limiting interpretability and systematic debugging. We introduce an easy-to-use, plug-and-play framework for concept-based interpretation and model refinement. By aligning a single-modality encoder to BioMedCLIP, we construct a Concept Bottleneck Model (CBM) that enables concept-level interventions. These interventions allow us to isolate causal versus spuriously correlated concepts, validate insights with domain experts, and generate counterfactual samples for targeted fine-tuning. We evaluate our framework on a Mayo Clinic ultrasound dataset and the CheXpert 5x200 chest X-ray dataset. Results demonstrate that concept intervention enables reliable model diagnosis while maintaining, and occasionally improving predictive performance via guided fine-tuning. Our findings highlight the practical value of this framework for controlled, interpretable refinement of clinical deep learning models.
